Sports.title: Paula Badosa hits back at ex-boyfriend Stefanos Tsitsipas after he revealed why he would NOT date another tennis star - following their high-profile split
Sports.content:
Paula Badosa left little room for interpretation of her feelings after ex-boyfriend and fellow tennis star Stefanos Tsitsipas said he would not date another player again.

Tennis's power couple - dubbed 'Tsitsidosa' by fans - called time on their romance for a second time back in July last year after being 'shattered' by the demands of their professional careers.

Tsitsipas has since moved on and is in a relationship with Kristen Thoms. Thoms is a tennis player turned model who ditched her sporting career after competing at college level.

Tsitsipas, formerly world No 3, was answering questions on social media and was asked whether his preference is to date a tennis player or non-tennis player.

He responded: 'Non-tennis girlfriend. Trust me. Even if you don’t want to admit there’s competitiveness, there’s always competitiveness.'

Evidently the feeling was mutual with Badosa reacting to her ex-boyfriend's comments with four laughing emojis on the post.

Stefanos Tsitsipas, who used to go out with fellow player Paula Badosa, insisted he would rather have a non-tennis girlfriend

Tsitsipas' mother, Julia, previously spoke about why the relationship did not work.

'Their relationship was complicated from beginning to end,' Julia told Serbian outlet Telegraf.

‘On the one hand, she distracted him from tennis, and on the other hand, the breakup hit him hard.

‘I was a professional tennis player and I thought that tennis players should not react so emotionally.

'Their relationship was not ordinary, everyday. They were in a long-distance relationship. Both entered the relationship traumatized by injuries. Paula didn't play at all when they started dating.

'But at no time was there a possibility that Stefanos would end his career because of their love.’

The couple initially broke up 'amicably' back in May 2024 but within three weeks they were back together and piquing the interest of fans all over again.

However by July last year they ended things again, with a source telling the mass-market Spanish magazine ¡Hola!: 'The breakup just happened. They both lost in the first round in London [at Wimbledon] and everything has come together for them.

Tsitsipas and Badosa split in July 2024 after a 'complicated' relationship which lasted a little over two years

Tsitsipas has revealed that he's found love again less than a year after splitting from Badosa, with Kristen Thoms (above)

'[They] were going through a rough patch professionally, with injuries, and that affected their relationship.

'They're not well, of course. It's normal for any couple that breaks up. They had started the year very well, and their dream has been shattered.

'It's a healthy breakup and there were no third parties or family influences, as is starting to be said.

'[They] have struggled to make their relationship work, but ultimately it hasn't worked out. Ghosts from the past have returned, marked by the injuries they have both suffered.

'[The split is] between adults who loved each other very much, and it was a mature decision.'

Badosa is setting up her own swimwear brand in a clear nod to thinking outside the court

Badosa and Tsitsipas unfollowed each other on social media and removed posts referring to each other.

And last November, Badosa confirmed the split as she held up a sash with the words 'Sexy and single' as she celebrated her 28th birthday with friends in Dubai.

The tennis star shared photos of her with a birthday cake reading 'older, wiser and still hotter than ever', along with another sash that stated '28 and still a 10'.

Sports.title: The moment that showed Anthony Joshua's tacit agreement to return to boxing in late summer: JEFF POWELL on what's next after Deontay Wilder beat Derek Chisora and why 'addicted' Brit should have been disqualified
Sports.content:
The moment that showed Anthony Joshua's tacit agreement to return to boxing in late summer: JEFF POWELL on what's next after Deontay Wilder beat Derek Chisora and why 'addicted' Brit should have been disqualified

Derek Chisora peeked over the precipice of retirement and blinked. Boxing covered its black eyes as the 42-year-old warhorse declined to confirm that it is 50 fights and out.

Deontay Wilder gave a sigh of relief as victory staved off that decision which all boxers dread. In his reawakened mind there are still world heavyweight titles to be won after 40.

Bless 'em, both. The adrenaline was still pumping a torrent after the exhilaration of a battle royale which offended the snootiest connoisseurs but raised the roof of the O2.

Chisora had promised his family and followers that he would hang up the gloves after Saturday night on the south bank of the Thames. Mrs Chisora, her husband conceded, will have to be consulted yet again. Although he warned her: 'I am addicted to boxing.'

Wilder, the demon puncher whose six-year reign as world champion was ended by Tyson Fury, is eyeing another hot night in London as his gateway to redemption. To that end he fist-pumped the onlooking Anthony Joshua by way of tacit agreement to a late summer showdown of Wembley Stadium potential.

What a difference a fight makes. Two old pros considered to be on their last legs put on the hottest show in town for many a night. The prime candidate for fight of the year, perhaps of this newish century.

Derek Chisora (left) could seemingly carry on his career despite insisting he will retire after warning he is 'addicted to boxing'

The return of Anthony Joshua (pictured), meanwhile, seems set for the summer with a potential fight with Deontay Wilder on the cards

It does not take two grand masters of the noble art to make a great fight. Del Boy and Deontay proved that by going at each other hammer and tongs for every one of the 12 rounds. Chisora somehow survived the distance while taking at least double that number of monstrous blows from the American recognised as the mightiest puncher since Mike Tyson. How on earth did he keep punching back?

Classy and stylish, this was not. Thrilling, exciting, blood rousing, compelling, entertaining, unrelenting and brutally phenomenal, it most certainly was.

A throwback to the bare-knuckle days of yore when men o' war stepped up to a line scratched into the ground and stood there battering each other to a bloodied pulp until one of them collapsed.

Despite his protestations that he won the fight, it was Chisora's face that showed the more vivid signs of combat, his legs that wobbled most often and he who was hammered twice through the ropes.

Two of the judges gave it to Wilder by respective scores of 115-111 and 115-113. The third card was 115-112 the other way. A split decision was generous to Chisora. I hate having to tell him after all his valiance but this correspondent scored it 117-111 to the Bronze Bomber, even after allowing for the one point deduction for Wilder for no apparent reason and including two even rounds.

That is not the only reason for supposing that referee Mark Bates was overwhelmed by so wild a brawl and the high-octane atmosphere it generated in the arena. There were plenty of visits to the canvas. So many that he appeared to lose count of how many were punch-inflicted and how many grappled and wrestled to the floor.

Most of us counted two legitimate knock downs by Wilder. Both when Chisora fell entangled in ropes which he criticised as too loose.

His objections to the result were trumped also by incidents that should have cost him the fight before he took all the punishment. He should have been disqualified when one of his corner-men climbed to his aid in the ring during a round. Then again when Mr Bates unforgivably helped him up from the ropes instead of counting over him.

Wilder and Chisora put on arguably the fight of the century on Saturday, with the Bronze Bomber winning by split dcision

Chisora did well to hang in there, but should twice have been disqualified during the fight

Not that the crowd would have wanted to be deprived of so much as a minute of this thriller.

As he ponders his future, Chisora might consider whether there will ever be a better night to bow out than this. On his shield of bravery but even more so on the rapturous acclaim of his followers that carried him into the night.

The affection for this cult idol of British boxing overflowed into an astonishing moment when his close American buddy Wilder, as he was about to belt him through the ropes, paused to tell him: 'I'm sorry. I love you.'



With friends like this, who needs enemies?

Sports.title: Derek Chisora and Deontay Wilder's heavyweight bout is marred by fans FIGHTING in the O2 Arena stands - as security step in to escort punters out
Sports.content:
Fight night on Saturday didn't just extend to Derek Chisora versus Deontay Wilder, as their heavyweight bout also saw several fans scrap among themselves during it in the stands.

Wilder emerged victorious during his entertaining encounter with Chisora via split decision (115-111, 112-115 and 115-113) at the O2 Arena.

But while the two were slugging it out in the ring, unsavoury scenes unfolded among a section of the crowd who exchanged their own punches.

In videos circulating on social media, several people can be seen throwing punches at each other.

One video on X, shows the melee unfolding before panning back to the boxing and then returning to the punching in the stands.

As the spectators unfurl their own haymakers on fellow punters, security staff can be seen wading in to break up the big scuffle.

Eventually they managed to physically drag some of those involved away and out of the event.

‼️Fight in the Crowd during Chisora vs Wilder‼️ pic.twitter.com/NJSswcdrlH — Bobby_LAD (@_BobbyLAD) April 5, 2026

A fight broke out in O2 Arena stands on Saturday during Derek Chisora versus Deontay Wilder

Security soon stepped in to break up the fight and escort some of the fans out of the O2 Arena

As for the actual heavyweight fight itself, Wilder (left) beat Chisora (centre) by split-decision

In another video, one of the fans can be seen being lifted out of his seat by security staff before being dragged away.

It is unclear at the moment if anyone was hurt following the unpleasant incident.

As for the actual boxing itself, the victorious Wilder claimed to move down the gears to help his friend before he extended an invite to the whole Chisora family to visit his home of Alabama.

'I knew Derek was going to come and bring everything that he had to fight,' the American said.

'I was telling him in the ring when his eyes swell and his temple start to bleed, I said, "bro, you've got to live for your kids, I don't want to hurt you too much longer," so I started having fun in there because I saw my brother going to get hurt.

'That's what boxing is not about. Too many lives have been lost in this ring and when it is over for us, no one gives a damn. I looked after Derek tonight and I didn't want to go too hard... I want him to live for his kids. It's time for us to take care of each other.'

As for Chisora, he refused to confirm if this would be his final fight in what has been a 19-year professional career.

'Erm, the boss lady is right here. Last fight?

Fight in the crowd, like there are at every boxing event 🤣 #ChisoraWilder pic.twitter.com/zBeNGzqTSu — Chewy (@Chewy9991) April 4, 2026

Speaking post-fight, Wilder claimed he stepped off the gas to prevent any damage to Chisora

'Yeah, so listen, the fight, did I lose it by one point or by two points? Yeah, because I came out of the ring but it is what it is. I'm going to go home with the boss lady and see wagwan.

'Thank you very much United Kingdom, I really appreciate you. I came here when I was 16, I was born in Zimbabwe, came here to visit my mother, I got into trouble, I started boxing and I didn't know I would be addicted to boxing.

'I kept on going, some of my peers have retired and left but thank you very much, I appreciate it (the support).'

Sports.title: Referee dives in to save glamorous UFC fighter after she is knocked out with a knee to the face and punched in the head on the floor
Sports.content:
Referee dives in to save glamorous UFC fighter after she is knocked out with a knee to the face and punched in the head on the floor

An MMA referee was forced to dive in and save a glamorous UFC fighter after she was knocked out cold with a knee to the face in her latest match.

Hailey Cowan, 34, found herself on the wrong end of a vicious attack by Alice Pereira at UFC Fight Night 272, and was punched in the head while on the floor before the referee dived in the way.

The bantamweight fight took place on the preliminary card, with veteran Cowan up against it versus up-and-coming fighter Pereira, 20.

She did, however, make it to the second round, and it was the fifth minute in which she received the knee to the face, which knocked her out and sent her to the canvas.

As is common in MMA, Pereira then pounced on her opponent in a bid to finish her off, but Keith Peterson jumped in to break it up as the Brazilian was declared the winner.

It took Pereira to a record of seven wins and one loss. She is the youngest-ever female fighter to win a fight in the UFC, and the youngest to score a knockout.

THE GOLDEN GIRL!



Alice Pereira knocks out Hailey Cowan with a vicious knee! 😤 #UFCVegas115 | Stream TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KNqlt8DhVd — UFC on TNT Sports (@ufcontnt) April 4, 2026

The referee was forced to step in and save glamorous UFC fighter Hailey Cowan after she was knocked out cold

Cowan, 34, lost her third-straight fight in the promotion after receiving a brutal knee to the face

The fighter (left) shows off her training routines and family life on her social media accounts

Cowan, however, was in good spirits post-fight, writing on Instagram: 'God is still good. I still have lots to smile about :) and I am just fine. Heartbroken, but blessed.

'Passion is what we do, purpose is why we do it. Thank you Jesus for the courage to do scary things and to dream big. Chin is still high.'

Cowan has been a pro fighter since 2018 and has a record of seven wins and five defeats. She has lost all three of her fights in the UFC, however, debuting against Jamey-Lyn Horth in 2023.



She boasts more than 50,000 followers on Instagram, sharing photos of her workouts and fights, while also giving an insight into her family life.

Sports.title: Liverpool 'gave up': Virgil van Dijk's startling admission as he apologises for Man City surrender - and says he and his team-mates must 'take a look at ourselves' to save their season
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk has apologised to Liverpool fans for a torrid display at Manchester City and says the team are letting down under-fire boss Arne Slot.

The Reds were thrashed 4-0 at the Etihad Stadium in the FA Cup quarter-final on Saturday and plenty of the 7,600 travelling supporters were long gone by full-time.

Captain Van Dijk says this season has been extremely tough – but the Dutchman has vowed to do all he can to put it right ahead of a defining Champions League tie against Paris Saint-Germain.

'I've been repeating myself too many times,' he said. 'Obviously, it goes out in the media because obviously I'm here all the time.

'We let our fans down today. We let ourselves down and the manager, but we let our fans down today.

Virgil van Dijk and Liverpool were sent crashing out of the FA Cup at the hands of Man City

'Up until the penalty, maybe not… but the way we played especially in the second half. That must hurt for everyone. It definitely hurts me. So the focus is now on Paris away, but it's tough. It will be a tough Sunday to digest it.

'I'll be with my son (on Sunday), so that's at least a good thing. Family at the end of the day is the most important thing, but other than that I am trying to think how we can turn it around but we have been going through this for almost 75 per cent of the season.

'Where we do well but we can't build on certain things and we fall back into games where we get beat on intensity or beat on how much you really want to go for it.

'It is a difficult one to take and everyone has to look at themselves. I am speaking for myself but it is mentally tough at the moment to take this.'

Van Dijk added: 'Obviously you come out of the dressing room with the right intentions to score and make it 2-1 and change the game, but the opposite happened and then to come back from 3-0 is obviously very difficult here. But also you shouldn’t give up, and that’s maybe what happened at a certain point.

'It is very difficult. Very difficult. But we have a responsibility, not only to ourselves but especially to the fans and, if we want to make something out of this season, we have to try and do something special in the next three games.'

Asked if the squad were still behind boss Slot, he said: 'Well, it's a together thing, isn't it? Obviously, he's responsible as the manager, but we are the ones on the pitch that have to do it.

'So, yeah, we... The matter of fact is now PSG is waiting for us. I watched them yesterday a little bit, and it will be so tough again. So we have to be ready mentally as soon as possible.

'I've been lucky enough to play for Liverpool for so many years and the main thing always was the togetherness.

'Now, obviously, we are in a little bit of a transition so we have to find it. It's still difficult to then perform each and every three days if we don't have it consistently if you know what I mean. The togetherness on the pitch to show it for 90 plus minutes every three or four days.

'That is difficult.'

Sports.title: Caitlin Clark's new WNBA salary revealed after breakthrough in talks and weeks of tense negotiations
Sports.content:
Caitlin Clark's new WNBA salary revealed after breakthrough in talks and weeks of tense negotiations

The remarkable salary increases of the WNBA's biggest stars have been laid bare after weeks of tense discussions with the league finally resulted in a new Collective Bargaining Agreement.

Caitlin Clark has been the face of the league since being drafted No 1 overall by the Indiana Fever in 2024, but her rookie contract paid her a paltry amount in comparison to her worth to the league.

Incredibly, Clark was earning just $85,000 a year for her first two seasons in the WNBA, gathering the majority of her wealth from sponsorship deals and other endeavors away from the basketball court.

All that is changing now, with base salaries skyrocketing not just for the current crop of WNBA stars, but also every new player joining the league - with the 2026 Draft happening in New York later this month.

Clark will earn a new salary of $528k in 2026, a remarkable 521% pay increase from her 2025 wage - all thanks to an 'EPIC' new clause, both in name and nature.

Caitlin Clark is being paid 521% more in 2026 than in 2025, in the wake of the new CBA

Clark has become the face of the WNBA in the two years since she was drafted at No 1 overall

The 'exceptional performance on initial contract' clause allows Clark to max out her possibilities on her four-year rookie deal, which still has two years to run before she can demand a much higher base salary from the Fever - or elsewhere.

The same clause also means that Clark is likely to only have one more season on her rookie deal, before she unlocks a lucrative extension.

Eligible players are those who win MVP or make the All-WNBA Team in their first three seasons, a category which Clark is set to fall into.

It's fair to say Clark may not have too many concerns about her bank balance, though, with Nike currently paying her $28 million over an eight-year deal.

Clark's new salary of $528k still pales in comparison to her worth to the WNBA, many believe

In March, Clark was also the face of Team USA in a series of World Cup qualifying games

Many believe that to have been a steal for the sportswear giants, tying down one of the world's top athletes for a relatively small fee in comparison to others.

Michael Jordan, for example, is said to still earn $60m annually from Nike, despite retiring from the NBA in 2003.

Meanwhile, some other big salary increases in the WNBA include Aliyah Boston, jumping from $94k to $574k, Paige Bueckers - from $80k to $500k - and Angel Reese - from $75k to $350k.



Clark's Indiana Fever teammate Boston, in fact, is set to be the WNBA's highest-paid player in 2026, with Dallas' Diamond Miller ($536,588) in second. Clark is third.

Sports.title: Former Champions League manager's football coach son abandons his team's derby to rush to his father's bedside as he 'has just days' to live and is in a coma after heart attack
Sports.content:
Iconic football manager Mircea Lucescu's condition is getting worse with the 80-year-old placed into an induced coma following a heart attack, with his son abandoning his side's derby match to be by his side.

The coach, who only left his role as Romania boss a matter of days ago, has been battling severe arrhythmias, which is a condition involving heart rhythm disturbances that can be life-threatening.

Reports stated that he suffered a heart attack on Friday morning, less than a week after he stepped down from his role at Romania after collapsing during a team meeting.

On Friday, a statement from the University Hospital in Bucharest said he was 'stable,' but reports in Romania say he now could only have days to live.

His family have rushed to be by his side, with his wife, Neli, and granddaughter Marilu present, while Razvan Lucescu, his son and manager of Greek side PAOK, has left his team during their derby clash with Panathinaikos to be at his bedside.

Mihai Stoichita, who works as a technical director of the Romania team, visited him in hospital and said he was unable to speak to his now-former colleague.

Mircea Lucescu is in a coma and has reportedly been given just days to live after a heart attack

The 80-year-old was Romania manager up until a matter of days ago and left his post after collapsing during a team meeting

He said: 'I can't give any news, because I haven't talked to anyone. I just sat there with him for about five minutes, he doesn't answer anything, that's normal. Let's hope he'll be fine, God willing.

'He can't talk. He's probably in an induced state to help, I know. I don't know how to tell him I don't understand. I just sat there and looked at him, that's all. I can't give any statement, because I'd probably say something stupid. He must have days, that's important, nothing else.

'Whoever it was, it hurts you, especially when you had a relationship with him. We were both adversaries and friends at the same time. I can't be either optimistic or pessimistic, because I'm not a doctor. I didn't say anything to him, I just touched him.

'Of course he is connected to the machines, he has extraordinary care, it is clear that someone is always checking. I have not spoken to any doctor. May God grant that he will be well, that he will live, that he will continue to be with us. Hope dies last.'

There were initially high hopes for Lucescu's recovery. He had undergone heart surgery and had a fifth stent fitted, which is used to help keep arteries open and increase blood flow.

He was said to have been sitting up and talking, but his condition has deteriorated over the last few hours.

Mircea Lucescu, who had a long playing career that saw him feature 64 times for Romania, started coaching in 1979 upon his retirement and first managed his country in 1981 until 1986.

After that, he had stints as boss of the likes of Inter Milan, Galatasaray and Besiktas, enjoying time as a Champions League boss.

His son, Razvan Lucescu, has left his side PAOK ahead of a derby clash to be with his father

The duo have both had long careers in football management, both coaching the Romania team

More recent jobs have seen him lead Turkey between 2017 and 2019 and Dynamo Kyiv from 2020 to 2023, while he rejoined Romania in 2024.

His son, Razvan, 57, also coached Romania between 2009 and 2011. Having also worked for the likes of Al Hilal, he took over at PAOK for the second time in 2021, but has had to leave his side without their head coach before their Greek play-off game against Panathinaikos.

The game will kick off at 5pm BST on Sunday.

Sports.title: Judd Trump takes emergency action for Tour Championship final as move dubbed 'risky'
Sports.content:
Judd Trump takes emergency action for Tour Championship final as move dubbed 'risky'

Judd Trump has been forced to take some drastic measures against his cue this week, and he had to do so again in his Tour Championship final clash against Zhao Xintong

View 3 Images Judd Trump has had a difficult time with his cue this week (Image: Tai Chengzhe, VCG via Getty Images)

Judd Trump was once again compelled to change the tip of his cue ahead of his Tour Championship final showdown with Zhao Xintong. The World No. 1 needed urgent attention on his cue during his recent triumph over Shaun Murphy.

‌



While he was falling behind to the Magician in their earlier encounter, Trump enlisted the help of his pal Charlie, who swiftly reshaped the top of his cue. It proved to be the turning point as he fought back and defeated Murphy in a nail-biting deciding frame.

‌



Come this Sunday, snooker legend Stephen Hendry spotted the Ace in the Pack tinkering with his cue once more - swapping out the tip. Speaking on Eurosport with the score level at 2-2, Hendry said: "We were looking at it in the green room and I think it is. It looks like a new tip.

‌



Judd Trump and figure skater girlfriend spark split rumours after snooker ace left homeless READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Maybe he thought the other one was just past its best and it was going to be no good today. It's a risk putting a new tip on the day before a final.

"But he's striking the ball well. A couple of deep screw backs he's done [well]. It was a risk but it might be paying off."

‌



View 3 Images Trump wanted everything to be perfect in his battle against Zhao (Image: Getty)

Following his match against Murphy, Trump hinted he might not have prevailed had his mate Charlie not turned up to repair his cue. He said: "Before that my cueing was all over the place.

"I didn't know where I was aiming. He shaped the tip and made it more reactive, I was able to get more power when I needed it."

‌



Given what Zhao accomplished against John Higgins in his semi-final encounter, Trump couldn't allow anything to be off form. The Cyclone swept Higgins aside, crushing the Scotsman 10-1.

View 3 Images Trump was behind 5-3 after the first session (Image: Photo by Tai Chengzhe/VCG via Getty Images)

Given the thrashing he received, it was perhaps unsurprising that Higgins tipped Zhao to claim the Tour Championship. He told reporters: "I think Xintong (will win).

Article continues below

"The way he plays, and how easy he wins frames, and just the way he goes about the patterns he's got. I think Xintong is favourite. He's that special a player, I think."

Sports.title: Tiger Woods' friends concerned by Vanessa Trump's advice as they turn on golfer's partner
Sports.content:
Tiger Woods' friends concerned by Vanessa Trump's advice as they turn on golfer's partner

Tiger Woods' friends are frustrated with his refusal to retire after the golf legend's charges for driving under the influence, property damage and refusing to submit to a test

View 2 Images Vanessa Trump is said to be supporting Tiger Woods' golf return (Image: James Gilbert/TGL, TGL Golf via Getty Images)

Tiger Woods' inner circle are both frustrated and worried by Vanessa Trump's inability to divert his attention from yet another comeback. Their concerns come after the golf legend's most recent car crash and golf return.

‌



Woods' Land Rover overturned after he clipped a lorry's trailer while making a last-ditch attempt to overtake. According to local sheriff John Budensiek, he was travelling at an excessive speed.

‌



The 15-time major champion faces charges of driving under the influence, property damage, and refusing to submit to a lawful test. Bodycam footage surfaced of Woods appearing to struggle while completing the standard cognitive tests.

‌



This latest scandal is a significant setback for Woods, personally and professionally, and has strained his romantic relationship with Trump. She has since broken her silence and reached a decision regarding their future together.

The couple have been an item since March, marking Trump's first serious relationship since her divorce from Donald Trump Jr. in March 2018. The crash has "raised some concerns" for her ex-husband.

New Tiger Woods footage shows golf icon asleep in police car minutes after arrest READ MORE :

Tiger Woods concern heightens as Jack Nicklaus issues emotional statement after arrest READ MORE :

Trump is equally wary of Woods' behaviour. However, according to a source speaking to The U.S. Sun, the golfer's closest friends are turning against Trump for fuelling his desire to mount another remarkable comeback.

‌



"Tiger has been completely obsessed with getting back to the top and becoming the player he once was - back in the spotlight alongside the biggest athletes in the world," the source said. "She's not grounding him or encouraging him to shift focus toward his family and business life.

"The pressure weighs heavily on him, and he hasn't accepted that he may never reach the top again. There is a level of denial."

The source added: "Most of his friends think he should retire and focus on his health, but he refuses to accept that other players have taken the spotlight. He constantly talks about his golden years and believes he can get back there. Some people stay quiet just to avoid upsetting him."

‌



"He constantly talks about his golden years and believes he can get back there. Some people stay quiet just to avoid upsetting him."

View 2 Images Vanessa Trump and Tiger Woods are a year into their relationship (Image: Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"She's frustrated with the negative publicity and has told him he can't bring that energy into the home or around the kids; she wants him to be an example - resilient, inspiring, and fully committed to becoming a top golfer again."

With his next court appearance scheduled for May, Woods has enlisted Douglas Duncan and reportedly plans to leave the United States to focus on his recovery. Duncan entered a not-guilty plea on Woods' behalf earlier this week.

Woods is preparing to step back from golf to aid his recuperation. In his first public statement since the crash, Woods took to social media to share the following message: "I know and understand the seriousness of the situation I find myself in today.

Article continues below

"I am stepping away for a period of time to seek treatment and focus on my health. This is necessary in order for me to prioritise my well-being and work toward lasting recovery.

"I'm committed to taking the time needed to return to a healthier, stronger, and more focused place, both personally and professionally. I appreciate your understanding and support, and ask for privacy for my family, loved ones and myself at this time."

Sports.title: Zhao Xintong stuns TV pundit during Tour Championship clash - 'You run out of things to say'
Sports.content:
Zhao Xintong stuns TV pundit during Tour Championship clash - 'You run out of things to say'

John Higgins lost to Zhao Xintong in the Tour Championship semi-finals, and the reigning world champion left snooker pundit Alan McManus lost for words at Manchester Central

View 2 Images Zhao Xintong was in imperious form against John Higgins (Image: Tai Chengzhe, VCG via Getty Images)

Zhao Xintong left Alan McManus and Matthew Stevens almost lost for words after thrashing John Higgins 10-1 in the Tour Championship semi-finals. The world champion reeled off nine consecutive frames during a commanding performance to set up Sunday's final against world number one Judd Trump.

‌



The 29-year-old executed one long pot early in the sixth frame with a red ball covering half the pocket. McManus described it as the finest shot that he had ever witnessed.

‌



The audience inside the Manchester Central Convention Complex erupted in applause following that remarkable moment. And McManus said: "He has been amazing again. How do you hurt him on the table, and how do you get to him mentally?

‌



"There is one shot in particular that, I believe, is the best shot I've ever seen; it was that good. He only has half a pocket, but he barely hits the cue ball; it is mesmerising. You run out of things to say. I am glad I was not in the comms box, as you would not know what to say."

And former UK champion Stevens concurred, saying: "He only had half a pocket to aim at. It is just like a laser, it is unbelievable. He is like a machine; it is fantastic to watch."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌

Stevens then added: "He is like watching a computer game; he literally does not miss anything easy. His long potting puts you under all sorts of pressure to get good safety. He just keeps knocking them in; you run out of things to say about him."

Zhao was understandably delighted with his display, saying: "I played well, and I am very happy to reach the final. My cueing was very good, I tried not to think too much – I just enjoyed the table and concentrated on the balls."

‌



"This season I have been in four finals. I am enjoying every moment and trying to get better.

View 2 Images Zhao Xintong thrashed John Higgins in their Tour Championship semi-final, losing just a single frame (Image: Getty)

"To play Judd in a final for the first time will be a big moment for me. It will be very tough."

Article continues below

Zhao has triumphed in all three of his finals this year, including defeating Higgins in the most recent one back in February. He claimed the Players Championship in Telford a fortnight after securing the World Grand Prix title in Hong Kong.

The final was the non-ranking Riyadh Season Championship in Saudi Arabia, where he overcame Neil Robertson back in November. Zhao also knocked out Trump in the semi-finals of that tournament late last year, winning 4-3, which remains their last encounter to date.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua ready to fight Deontay Wilder after ringside call-out
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua ready to fight Deontay Wilder after ringside call-out

Anthony Joshua ran into Deontay Wilder on Saturday night after watching the American beat Derek Chisora

View Image Deontay Wilder called out Anthony Joshua for a blockbuster fight

Anthony Joshua is willing to put his money-spinning clash with Tyson Fury at risk by facing Deontay Wilder this summer.

‌



Joshua watched Wilder edge out Derek Chisora on Saturday night in his first public appearance since he was involved in a tragic car crash last December. The former heavyweight world champion has been recuperating since the smash which killed his close friends Sina Ghami and Latif Ayodele.

‌



But Joshua is now back in training and has pencilled in his return for July. And after witnessing Wilder drop Chisora en route to a split-decision points victory, the Brit is ready to finally settle their long-running rivalry. The pair held talks in 2018 when they both held versions of the world championship but a $50million deal collapsed.

‌



Derek Chisora LOSES to Deontay Wilder in bonkers final fight READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua gives Deontay Wilder ice-cold stare as rivals cross paths READ MORE :

And contracts were signed in 2023 for a two-fight dust-up only for Wilder to lose to Joseph Parker to leave the plan in ruins. The American crossed paths with Joshua as he left the ring on Saturday and demanded: "Now let's get it on". At 40, Wilder is past the peak of his devastating powers and was unable to knock out Chisora in the Brit's farewell fight.

He will also undergo scans on his right hand amid fears he fractured it during his 45th career victory. But should he and Joshua strike a deal, Wilder still possesses the power to wreck the long-awaited Battle of Britain. Fury will end his 16-month hiatus from the ring on Saturday night against Arslanbek Makhmudov with Joshua expected to be in attendance.

Article continues below

Wilder, meanwhile, claimed he went EASY on Chisora to ensure he retired with his health intact. Chisora will hang up his gloves after his 50th professional fight ended in defeat. And Wilder said: "He has fought everyone, so why not retire? Even in the ring I was thinking about his retirement. My team were telling me to push forward but I held back a couple of times.

"When I cut his eye I started thinking about him being with his children. When I saw veins coming out of his temple, I started thinking that this is a dangerous sport. I felt a little sympathy for him. I was even talking to him, like, 'Derek, come on, we need to stop this, man, we need to stop this'."

Sports.title: Mo Salah and Virgil van Dijk slammed after Liverpool horror show - 'This is unprecedented'
Sports.content:
Mo Salah and Virgil van Dijk slammed after Liverpool horror show - 'This is unprecedented'

Mohamed Salah and Virgil van Dijk both started and disappointed as Arne Slot's Liverpool were dumped out of the FA Cup after being hammered 4-0 by Man City on Saturday

View 2 Images Mohamed Salah was poor during Liverpool's FA Cup defeat to Man City (Image: ( Marc Atkins/Getty Images))

Liverpool icon Steve Nicol has slammed Mohamed Salah for his performance against Manchester City. The forward endured an afternoon to forget at the Etihad as his side were dumped out of the FA Cup.

‌



Making his last appearance for the Reds against Pep Guardiola’s side, the forward missed two good chances in either half as well as seeing a penalty saved by James Trafford during the 4-0 defeat. A hat-trick from Erling Haaland and a well-taken finish from Antoine Semenyo condemned Arne Slot’s side to another defeat.

‌



Salah will leave Liverpool during the summer after reaching an agreement with the club to end his contract early. And Nicol, speaking on ESPN FC, believes the forward’s decline this season is unprecedented.

‌



He said: “This is unprecedented. How can you go from almost winning the Player of the Year last year to this? To the fact that now you don’t look as though you know where the goal is.”

Reflecting on Salah’s second-half miss, the five-time league winner with the Reds said: “The fact is, he had plenty of time to get it under control and pick his spot. But his touch is so poor.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Virgil van Dijk issues damning verdict after Man City thrashing leaves Liverpool reeling READ MORE :

“Where’s the power? He’s obviously, his whole body shape’s wrong. And even the penalty kick. He doesn’t have his head up. You watch the majority of people take penalty kicks nowadays.

“They’re all watching where the goalie is. But Mo is so concentrated and so unsure that he has to concentrate on the ball and make sure he gets a good strike.

“And so all that other stuff that you would normally do with your head up, because you’re confident, has completely and utterly disappeared.”

‌



Virgil van Dijk was another Liverpool player who endured an afternoon to forget against Guardiola's side as he was guilty of giving away a first-half penalty. And speaking alongside Nicol, former Chelsea defender Craig Burley took aim at Van Dijk, saying: “He’s been poor as well.

View 2 Images Liverpool were hammered by Man City (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

“Two guys that were paid a King’s ransom in the summer, two leaders, he’s the captain, two guys that have taken this Liverpool team on their shoulders in different aspects, have been two of the worst performers.

‌



“Obviously, [Ibrahima] Konate has had a very, very bad season, but in terms of leadership, positioning and defending with Van Dijk’s quality, he’s been poor.”

Reflecting on the defeat, Van Dijk said: “Very difficult - very difficult to accept, very difficult to be out there. Very tough day and I feel bad for the fans as well."

Sports.title: Julian Alvarez Arsenal links blasted as club chief says 'you're going a bit overboard'
Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez Arsenal links blasted as club chief says 'you're going a bit overboard'

Julian Alvarez has been strongly linked to a transfer away from Atletico Madrid, with Arsenal and Barcelona as potential suitors

View 2 Images Atletico Madrid present has sent a clear message to any Julian Alvarez transfer suitors (Image: (Photo by Bruno Penas/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images))

Atletico Madrid president Enrique Cerezo has hit out at the Spanish media over speculation linking Julian Alvarez with a move away from the club. Arsenal are among a host of sides to have emerged as an interested party with Barcelona as another club linked.

‌



Ahead of the two clubs' La Liga clash on Saturday evening, Cerezo delivered an unequivocal message to the assembled press. He said: "You are crossing the line a little with Alvarez. He's an Atletico Madrid player and has a long contract with the club."

‌



Barcelona went on to claim victory in that encounter, with Robert Lewandowski - the very player Alvarez would be expected to replace should he make the switch - netting a late winner from the bench. Marcus Rashford had earlier levelled after Giuliano Simeone's opener.

‌



Alvarez did not make it off the bench for the fixture, with Atleti's attentions firmly fixed on the Champions League, as they now trail leaders Barcelona by 19 points. A quarter-final showdown between the two Spanish giants is set to unfold over the coming weeks, with Alvarez seemingly being kept fresh for Wednesday's first leg at Camp Nou.

It has been another prolific campaign for the Argentine, who currently boasts 17 goals from 44 appearances. He notched 29 in his debut season under Diego Simeone, and matching that tally remains within reach with Atletico still having a maximum of 15 matches left to play.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Arsenal's interest comes as little surprise, given sporting director Andrea Berta was likely instrumental in negotiating his £82million transfer from Manchester City. Despite Viktor Gyokeres finding the net in the FA Cup quarter-final defeat at the hands of Southampton, Arsenal's struggles in front of goal were once again laid bare.

Arteta's side have now endured back-to-back damaging cup exits, with a crucial run of fixtures looming that could well shape their entire season. A Champions League quarter-final first leg away to Sporting CP comes first, followed by a Premier League fixture against Bournemouth at Emirates Stadium the following weekend.

View 2 Images Arsenal must respond to their recent cup defeats

‌



A few days later, the Gunners remain in north London for the second leg against the Portuguese side, before a potentially decisive title race showdown against Manchester City at Etihad Stadium.

Should Arsenal progress past Sporting, a Champions League semi-final awaits against either Barcelona or Alvarez's Atletico Madrid. The latter netted three times in the previous round against Tottenham, yet was kept remarkably quiet when facing the Gunners in the group stages, with Arteta's men running out convincing 4-0 winners.

Barcelona's defensive frailties would also make Arsenal firm favourites for a potential semi-final against Hansi Flick's side, despite their contrasting fortunes in attack, with Newcastle having been thrashed 7-2 in the second leg of their last-16 tie.

Sports.title: Man Utd handed timely injury boost as Michael Carrick to welcome back star
Sports.content:
Man Utd handed timely injury boost as Michael Carrick to welcome back star

Manchester United have been without Patrick Dorgu since late January due to a hamstring injury and the left winger is making good progress in his recovery at Carrington

View 2 Images Michael Carrick will have Patrick Dorgu back fit soon (Image: Matt Impey/Shutterstock)

Patrick Dorgu is making good progress in his recovery from a hamstring injury in a major boost to Michael Carrick. The Manchester United winger has been sidelined since picking up the injury in the 3-2 away win at Arsenal on January 25.

‌



Dorgu was expected to be out for around 10 weeks with the injury, which came after he scored against the Gunners. The Denmark international was a revelation in the early days of Carrick's interim spell and will provide another option on the left flank once he returns.

‌



He has missed eight games so far and the Premier League match against Leeds on April 13 was slated as a target return date after the initial prognosis. It is understood that the Leeds game will come too soon for Dorgu, but United announced on Saturday that he has returned to the grass at their Carrington training ground, working individually.

‌



The 21-year-old has been undergoing meticulous strength and conditioning training in an effort to get back into the side. United only have seven matches remaining this season, with securing a place in next season's Champions League their sole goal.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd could have upper hand in £100million fight thanks to strict transfer rule READ MORE :

Bruno Fernandes names Premier League star who should replace him at Man Utd READ MORE :

They sit third in the Premier League table, having won seven of the 10 games under Carrick's management, taking 23 from a possible 30 points. In truth, United haven't missed Dorgu, with Carrick shuffling his pack to place Matheus Cunha to the left of attack to cover, but his form before he got injured won't have been forgotten.

‌



Dorgu scored in the 1-0 win over Newcastle on Boxing Day, in the 2-0 win over Manchester City on January 17 and in the stunning 3-2 victory over league-leaders Arsenal on January 25.

"Pat’s been a big player for us, obviously he’s scored two goals but in terms of the threat and athleticism and quality, he’s been immense down the side with Luke [Shaw] against two teams that ask a lot of questions," Carrick said after the win over Arsenal.

View 2 Images Patrick Dorgu sustained a hamstring injury in Manchester United's win over Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“I am delighted for him because the two goals he’s scored are very different goals. It’s nice to see him smiling and happy.”

Gary Neville summed up his form on Sky Sports: "Patrick Dorgu looked like such an average wing-back under Ruben Amorim. Further forward he looks like a completely and utterly different player."

Dorgu has three goals and three assists in 22 Premier League appearances this season, having played as a left wing-back under Amorim before being pushed forward to become a conventional left winger under Carrick.

Article continues below

He has been on the sidelines with Matthijs de Ligt, who has been frustratingly out with a back injury. The Netherlands international has not played since the 2-1 win over Crystal Palace on November 30.

Sports.title: Arsenal sensation admits he 'shouldn't have been in England squad' amid injury debate
Sports.content:
Arsenal sensation admits he 'shouldn't have been in England squad' amid injury debate

Jack Wilshere's England career was on and off as injuries cost him multiple caps and the ex-Arsenal star admits some will deem him lucky to have played at two major tournaments

View 2 Images Jack Wilshere is proud of his England career, but injuries cost hm dear

Former Arsenal star Jack Wilshere admits there's an argument he "shouldn't have been in England squads" that went to major tournaments with his international career marred by injuries.

‌



The former Gunner burst onto the scene as a teenager and made his England debut in August 2010 at the age of 18. There was huge excitement over what he could deliver on the international stage, but a lack of fitness restricted him to just 34 caps.

‌



That didn't stop him from playing at the World Cup in 2014 and the Euros two years later. Wilshere had the faith of then boss Roy Hodgson, who was prepared to pick the Arsenal midfielder even if he had lacked minutes in the months leading up to those tournaments.

‌



Wilshere's quality wasn't in doubt, but fitness meant he was never playing his best when it came to representing the Three Lions on the international stage. He played in the infamous 2-1 loss to Iceland and the player himself admits that some will oppose him being selected.

The told The Telegraph: “I look back on my England career and those 34 caps could easily have been 75 – even if you cut down half the injuries. I look back with pride. I went to the World Cup and I went to the Euros. Probably didn’t get the best out of me because both were off the back of a season with bad injuries, but I had a coach in Roy Hodgson who I really liked.

Mikel Arteta issues immediate Arsenal demand after shock FA Cup exit to Southampton READ MORE :

“Arguably, I shouldn’t have been in those squads, but he trusted me. Sometimes I look back and think of what might have been. But I have really good memories of scoring two goals [against Slovenia in June 2015]; of having a run in the team as a No 6. I loved that. So, yeah, frustrating, but also really proud.”

‌



Wilshere would only score twice for his country, both of those screamers in a comeback win against Slovenia. Both goals saw the former Arsenal man take aim from range, with both strikes ending up in the top corner.

View 2 Images The former Arsenal man played at two major tournaments

Injury ultimately stopped Wilshere from ever reaching his true potential and he's now a manager at Luton. He's watching on as the next Arsenal academy product, Max Dowman, grabs the headlines. The 16-year-old recently became the Premier League's youngest ever scorer.

‌



And Wilshere would take him to the World Cup - insisting other nations wouldn't hold him back. “The only thing I would say is, Spain would take him. That’s what I think," he said.

"We have this way at times in England of building them up but then protecting them. You get caught in that [place]: ‘If he goes what will people say?’ He [Dowman] is definitely good enough. Even if he goes and he doesn’t play that much. Which I think he can. I think he is good enough."
